The Four Lakes Task Force said work at Smallwood Dam had reached a stage where the lake could begin filling again, even as construction continues at the other dam sites. “We are excited to meet this critical milestone in restoring the Four Lakes system,” Task Force President Dave Kepler said, as quoted by Midland Daily News.Before water began returning, crews completed most of the remaining work needed to prepare the dam. This included installing pipes and electrical systems and strengthening areas around the main and backup routes that allow water to pass through the dam. With that work completed, Smallwood Lake has now moved into the next stage of the project which is refilling.The progress at Smallwood comes as crews continue rebuilding the other damaged dams in the Four Lakes system.At Secord Dam, however, the planned completion date has been pushed back to November. The delay came after crews found a problem while installing one of the large gates used to control water flow. The gate had passed quality checks before leaving the manufacturer, but two parts did not fit together correctly when workers tried to install it.Other work at Secord Dam is continuing. Crews are working on the building that will house the dam's control systems, while work on the main spillway is nearing completion. A gate used to control water released through the lower part of the dam has also been installed.The delay has not changed the planned date for the lake to begin refilling at Secord. Kepler said the Task Force still expects to start the refill on April 15, 2027.Work is also continuing at Edenville Dam, where crews are preparing for more construction on the main structures that control water flow.At the Tittabawassee River section of the project, crews are nearing the end of another stage of work. The river has been redirected through a temporary channel, allowing workers to remove existing structures and begin building new sections of the dam.Construction is also continuing on the Tobacco River side. Crews are working on the structure that will control the movement of water and are continuing concrete and reinforcement work.The three dams are therefore at different stages of the rebuilding process. Smallwood has reached the point where its lake can begin filling, Secord is moving towards completion with some work delayed, and Edenville remains under construction.The Four Lakes Task Force is also helping property owners prepare for the return of the lakes. An in-person training session called 'How to build your natural shoreline' is scheduled for August 25 from 6 to 8 pm. The session will teach property owners about ways to create and protect natural shorelines.Property owners with eligible shoreline restoration projects can also apply for the Task Force's cost-share programme. The programme can help pay for natural shoreline improvements on private property.The Task Force will hold a public information session on October 7 to cover construction at Secord, Smallwood and Edenville dams, along with project finances and information about the lake refill process.
Article Summary: Six years after a catastrophic dam disaster left Smallwood Lake drawn down in Michigan, water is finally returning to the lake. The refill began on August 4, following the completion of a $50.2 million rebuild of Smallwood Dam. The project will restore the lake for 721 waterfront properties.

Article Title: Texas man who made his fortune selling vacuums, bought 5,500 acres in 1969 and spent 40 years restoring its grasslands, water and wildlife
Article Text:
PC: Selah, Bamberger Ranch Preserve

How Bamberger turned a fortune from business into a decades-long Texas land restoration project

PC: Selah, Bamberger Ranch Preserve

Turning damaged ranchland into healthy habitat

How healthier land brought dormant springs back to life

Wildlife returned as the habitat changed

How habitat restoration brought endangered species back

The artificial cave that sat empty for years

The ranch became a classroom for other landowners

What began in 1969 became a conservation legacy

A drive through the Texas Hill Country can make the landscape appear almost timeless. Limestone ridges rise above open grassland, scattered trees break up the horizon and streams cut through the valleys. But the appearance can hide a very different history.When J. David Bamberger went looking for ranchland in 1969, he was not interested in buying a beautiful, finished property. He wanted what he called the worst piece of land he could find. As reported by Selah Bamberger Ranch Preserve, he eventually bought 3,000 acres in Blanco County, near Johnson City, with a very specific purpose: to see whether badly overgrazed and neglected land could be brought back to functional health. Over the years, he added adjoining parcels until the property reached 5,500 acres. What followed became one of Texas' largest private habitat restoration projects. The transformation would take decades, requiring patience, careful management and a willingness to let damaged ecosystems gradually recover on their own terms.Bamberger's path to the Texas Hill Country was unusual. Born in rural Ohio in 1928, he grew up in poverty and developed an early interest in nature and land restoration through his mother, Hester.She gave him Louis Bromfield's Pleasant Valley, a book about restoring a worn-out farm. The story stayed with him. Years later, when Bamberger had built enough financial security to pursue his own ambitions, the idea returned in a very different setting.Reportedly, after moving to Texas with his young family in 1950, Bamberger worked as a vacuum cleaner salesman. He eventually went into business with fellow salesman Bill Church, helping build what became Church's Fried Chicken. When the company went public in 1969, Bamberger became wealthy enough to pursue his long-held ambition of restoring damaged land. Rather than spending his money on a polished ranch, he went looking for land that had already been pushed beyond its productive limits.The property Bamberger found had been heavily affected by years of grazing. Ashe juniper, commonly called cedar locally, had become widespread, while native grasses were scarce. Erosion had damaged the soil, and the ranch had virtually no usable surface water.The land was so dry that Bamberger tried drilling wells. Seven wells, each reaching about 500 feet, failed to produce water. The problem appeared to be much larger than simply finding a new water source. The landscape itself had lost much of its ability to capture and retain rainfall.The restoration team selectively removed Ashe juniper, replanted native grasses and altered the way the land was managed. Terraces and other water-management measures helped slow runoff, giving rainfall more opportunity to soak into the ground.The aim was not to eliminate every tree or turn the ranch into an artificial grassland. It was to create a wider mixture of habitats, including grasslands, oak savannah, riparian areas and remaining cedar thickets. Today, about 15 per cent of the preserve remains cedar thicket.One of the clearest signs that the restoration was working came from underground. As native grasses returned and runoff was reduced, long-dormant springs began flowing again. The preserve now has numerous springs, ponds and other water sources, and Miller Creek originates on the property before flowing toward the Pedernales River and eventually the Colorado River.The main spring produces an average of about three gallons of water per minute, enough to supply the ranch's water needs. Its overflow, together with other springs and seeps, contributes to the headwaters of Miller Creek. That made the project more than a story about restoring a scenic ranch. The preserve's restoration has been recognised by organisations including the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department, which awarded Bamberger the Lone Star Land Steward recognition, as well as the Leopold Conservation Award and other conservation organisations.The transformation was also visible in the animals using the property. Early bird surveys in the late 1960s and early 1970s recorded fewer than 50 species. As reported, the preserve's current records list 221 bird species, a dramatic increase that the ranch uses as one measure of improving habitat conditions.The recovery was not limited to birds. White-tailed deer on the original ranch were described as small and unhealthy because the available forage was limited. Bamberger's own account recorded average field-dressed weights of about 55 pounds in the early years. With greater habitat diversity and improved forage, bucks later averaged around 120 pounds, with a 156-pound record reported in 2013.The change reflected something deeper than larger animals. The ranch was producing a broader range of food and shelter, allowing wildlife to use different parts of the landscape throughout the year.As the habitat improved, Bamberger began looking at species that needed more than simply a healthier landscape. The preserve provides habitat for the endangered golden-cheeked warbler and the black-capped vireo. Neither species had been documented on the ranch before restoration began, while nesting pairs of golden-cheeked warblers have since been repeatedly recorded there.The ranch also became involved in the conservation of the scimitar-horned oryx, an antelope that had disappeared from the wild in the Sahara. Bamberger maintained a managed population and worked with zoos, including exchanges of breeding males intended to help maintain genetic diversity. Another unusual project involved bats.In 1998, Bamberger built a large artificial cave into a hillside for Mexican free-tailed bats. The structure was designed to accommodate as many as a million bats. But construction did not mean the animals would automatically arrive. For years, the cave remained empty. Hundreds of thousands of Mexican free-tailed bats began using the structure during the summer. The cave was named the Chiroptorium, a reference to Chiroptera, the scientific order that contains bats.The project captured the broader philosophy behind the ranch. Bamberger was not simply trying to preserve whatever remained. He was experimenting with ways to create conditions under which wildlife could return and thrive.By the time the transformation was well established, the preserve had become more than a private restoration project. Its mission expanded toward education, research and land stewardship. The preserve now describes itself as a place where landowners can learn conservation-oriented management by seeing the results on the ground. It hosts workshops, educational programmes, research partnerships and tours.His own financial success gave him the ability to take on a 5,500-acre project, but he argued that smaller landowners could apply the same principles. Removing unwanted growth, planting native species, improving water retention and using available equipment could all make a difference. The central idea was patience.In 2002, Bamberger and his wife, Margaret, established the Bamberger Ranch Preserve as a nonprofit organisation to protect the property from future development and maintain its conservation and educational work. The ranch continues to operate as a research and education resource as well as a restored landscape.
Article Summary: J. David Bamberger bought 3,000 acres in Blanco County, near Johnson City, in 1969. He wanted to see whether badly overgrazed and neglected land could be brought back to functional health. The transformation would take decades, requiring patience, careful management and a willingness to let damaged ecosystems gradually recover.

Article Title: US debt crosses $40 trillion but everyone still trusts Uncle Sam. But for how long?
Article Text:
US national debt crossed $40 trillion, exceeding annual GDP, as interest payments approach $1 trillion, with economists warning of painful adjustments ahead.

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Surprisingly, America is not mainly borrowing from China. The biggest lenders are actually Americans and American institutions – pension funds, mutual funds, banks, insurance companies, households and investment funds. Foreign governments and investors also buy what is euphemistically called “US Treasury securities”: Japan held about $1.12 trillion in June, Britain about $940 billion, China about $633 billion and India roughly $200 billion.

Yes, Uncle Sam, we’ll take your IOU.

The United States’ national debt crossed $40 trillion on Tuesday, a number so large that even breaking it up with commas can scarcely make it comprehensible. As in a 4 followed by 13 zeroes: $40,000,000,000,000!Number-crunching economists reached for various metrics to convey the scale of the crisis. The US economy produces roughly $33 trillion worth of goods and services a year. So the debt is now bigger than the entire annual economic output (GDP) of the country. Per American, that works out to roughly $118,000; for a family of four, about $472,000. Divvying it another way, the US is adding debt at a rate of roughly $90,000 every second.To put that in perspective for readers in India, the $40 trillion debt America has racked up is roughly 10 times the size of India’s entire annual economy. In other words — although debt versus GDP is not an apples-to-apples comparison — the US owes roughly ten times the value of everything India produces in a year. America’s debt mountain is therefore not merely bigger than India’s economy; it is about ten Indian economies stacked on top of one another.Economists also put the best possible spin by pointing out that the raw number itself is less important than debt relative to the size of the economy and the government’s ability to service it.Just the US debt held by its public is roughly equal to annual GDP, and the Congressional Budget Office says that, under current law, the ratio could rise to 120% of GDP by 2036 and 175% by 2056.So how did the world’s richest country get here? In the simplest terms, Washington has been spending more than it collects in taxes — year after year, administration after administration. Wars, tax cuts, the 2008 financial crisis, Covid stimulus, an ageing population and rising Social Security and Medicare costs have all added to the bill. The pandemic was particularly spectacular: debt exploded as the government tried to prevent an economic catastrophe.But the extraordinary thing is that America has continued borrowing heavily even after the emergencies have passed. Federal budget deficits are still running at levels normally associated with wars or recessions. The awkward question for Washington now is whether the borrowing eventually stops gently — or with a crash.So who is lending America $40 trillion?But why lend to a country this deeply in debt? Because US “Treasury securities” remain the world’s favourite financial equivalent of a steel safe with a very large lock. They are highly liquid, easily traded and backed by the world’s largest economy — as well as by Washington’s long-established record of paying its debts. In other words, America has been able to borrow on an extraordinary scale because the world keeps saying:For now.President Trump has repeatedly promised to reduce the national debt, including by using tariff revenue. But the arithmetic has not exactly been taking orders from the White House. Amid the irresistible American urge to splurge, Trump is proposing a $1.5 trillion military budget, roughly a 50% increase from recent levels and an unprecedented level of Pentagon spending, arguing that a stronger military is essential to national security.So America is essentially trying to lose weight while ordering a second dessert; spending like a drunken sailor on shore leave — and then promising the bartender that tariffs will somehow pay the tab.And debt is not merely about the amount borrowed. It is also about the interest bill. Interest payments are now approaching $1 trillion a year. That means an increasing share of the federal budget is going simply toward servicing yesterday’s borrowing rather than paying for today’s schools, roads, defence, healthcare or anything else Washington wants to spend money on.As the debt grows, investors could eventually demand higher interest rates to keep buying Treasury securities. That would feed through into mortgage rates, business borrowing costs and the government’s own financing costs, potentially slowing investment and economic growth. The US would then face the unpleasant menu economists have been warning about for years: higher taxes, slower spending, cuts to benefits, faster economic growth, inflation — or some combination of all of them.Washington would have to bring spending and revenues into better balance: restrain the growth of entitlement programmes, control discretionary spending, reconsider tax cuts, raise more revenue and — hardest of all — persuade voters that there is no painless option. There is no magic button marked “Pay Off $40 Trillion.”The CBO’s is essentially warning that the longer Washington waits, the more painful the eventual adjustment becomes. That is America’s peculiar fiscal paradox: the world’s richest country can afford an enormous debt — until one day the debt becomes so enormous that it starts deciding what the world’s richest country can afford. Or as one economist might put it, there is no such thing as a free lunch -- just a lunch somebody has put on the national credit card.
Article Summary: America is not mainly borrowing from China. The biggest lenders are actually Americans and American institutions. Japan held about $1.12 trillion in June, Britain about $940 billion, China about $633 billion and India roughly $200 billion.

Article Title: Atlanta Waffle House cook's rap praising the chain topped 1 million TikTok views; weeks later, he says he was fired after 20 years with the company
Article Text:
Waffle House cited repeated violations of its policy on unauthorised filming. (Facebook/theroundup)

‘Waffy Options’ becomes viral hit

He wanted 'Waffy Options' to be played on Waffle House jukeboxes across the chain.

Company says Riley broke rules

Riley says he was promoting restaurant

Riley turns to music after firing

Edric Riley, known to Waffle House customers and co-workers as Rockstar Riley, became an online sensation after a rap song celebrating the restaurant chain went viral. His song 'Waffy Options' crossed more than 1 million views on TikTok and received hundreds of thousands of views and shares on Instagram.But weeks after the song brought him popularity, his long association with Waffle House came to an end. Riley said he was fired from a restaurant in Sandy Springs, Georgia, on Friday after the company found that he had repeatedly broken its rules on filming promotional content on company property, Atlanta News first reported.Riley had worked at Waffle House on and off since he was a teenager. He told CBS News in July that he had been with the company for 20 years and had worked in several roles. His connection with the restaurant began when he was just 15.“I tried calling everyone. I couldn't get a ride, but I knew no matter what, I wanted that job,” Riley said. He recalled riding five miles on his mother’s bike to get to the restaurant after trying for eight months to get hired.“I'd been trying for eight months. So I got my mom's bike, put on some shorts and a T-shirt, grabbed my little sister's pink iPod Nano, loaded it with music and rode five miles.I've been rocking out at Waffle House ever since.”That long relationship later became the subject of the music Riley created about the chain. The project eventually reached a much bigger audience, with one song becoming particularly popular online.Riley said he wrote his first Waffle House song in September 2025. He recorded it in January and released it around February or March.“Waffy Options” was inspired by the restaurant, its food and the experience of working there. In the video that spread online, Riley appeared in his Waffle House uniform and performed behind the counter while customers and staff watched.The song praised the chain’s menu and its reputation for staying open when other restaurants are closed. Riley also encouraged people to visit their local Waffle House.His stage name, Rockstar Riley, became familiar to customers and co-workers, while another nickname, the “King of Waffle House”, appeared in coverage of his online success.The attention grew quickly. CBS News reported in July that Waffy Options had received more than 1 million TikTok views, along with hundreds of thousands of views and shares on Instagram.At the time, Riley had hoped the songs could become part of the restaurant experience. He wanted “Waffy Options” and his other tracks to be played on Waffle House jukeboxes across the chain’s more than 2,000 locations.“Please, everyone, keep going to Waffle House and tell them how much you love the music and the food,” Riley said in July. “Tell them you want to hear 'Waffy Options' and all the other great Waffle House songs on the jukebox.”Riley was fired on Friday from a Waffle House location in Sandy Springs. Waffle House said the decision was based on repeated violations of its policy against unauthorised filming of promotional media content on company property.“Waffle House ended its employment relationship with Mr. Riley following repeated violations of company policy prohibiting unauthorized filming of promotional media content on company property,” the company said in a statement to Atlanta News First.Waffle House said it supports employees who pursue creative work outside their jobs. However, it said company property cannot be used for personal promotion, commercial gain or brand monetisation without permission.The company said management had spoken to Riley several times about the policy and warned him that further violations could result in termination.According to Waffle House, Riley later filmed a music video in a restaurant parking lot without permission. The company said he brought a production crew, lighting and backup dancers for the shoot.“Candidly, we did everything we could to help him keep his job, but because of these repeated policy violations, he left us no choice,” Waffle House said.Riley has disputed the way the policy was applied and said he was disappointed by the decision. He said his music was created out of his love for both his work and his art. He also questioned whether the company's policy had been enforced equally.“I’m not out here taking purses, I’m not out here selling drugs. I’m just out here promoting the company that I worked for for 20 years in the most positive light,” Riley said. “You have a policy, so if you’re going to enforce it, it’s supposed to be enforced on everyone.”Riley said the firing was especially difficult because Waffle House had been his first job as a teenager. He had previously described the restaurant as a place where he had spent much of his working life.Despite losing his job, Riley said he would still be interested in working with Waffle House if the opportunity came. “I’m not going to lie, if that opportunity came, I would love to do it hands down,” Riley said. “I love Waffle House.”Following his termination, Riley said music producers and artists had contacted him about possible collaborations. He has also launched a GoFundMe campaign to help with living expenses and studio time while he pursues music full time.In the fundraiser, Riley said he had given Waffle House years of “loyalty, hard work, and dedication”. He also said he believed his viral video had helped bring attention to the chain.“Instead of feeling supported or appreciated, I was let go. After everything I poured into that job, this has been painful, disappointing, and honestly hard to process,” he wrote in the fundraiser. The campaign had raised more than $1,700, according to the New York Post.
Article Summary: Edric Riley, known to customers and co-workers as Rockstar Riley, became an online sensation after a rap song celebrating the restaurant chain went viral. His song 'Waffy Options' crossed more than 1 million views on TikTok and received hundreds of thousands of views and shares on Instagram. Riley said he was fired from a restaurant in Sandy Springs, Georgia, on Friday after the company found that he had repeatedly broken its rules on filming promotional content on company property.

Article Title: Help us: 4 Indian-origin teens from New Jersey call 911 during Mount Lafayette hike; they will have to pay a hefty fine for 'unprepared' adventure
Article Text:
Teerth Shah and Advik Yadav recount their hiking experience during which they had to call 911.

Four Indian-origin teenagers from New Jersey, Jainam Bhavsar, Purva Jayani, Tirth Shah and Advik Yadav, set out on an evening hike in New Hampshire, which proved to be costly for them. Though they were all safe and back home and did not require any medical assistance, they may have to pay a hefty fine for calling 911 to rescue them. The incident took place last Friday and they were rescued Saturday after a nine-hour operation by the emergency team.The first mistake they made was to start late. According to local reports, they did not start hiking until 3.30 pm which was less than 4.5 hours before sunset. NBC reported that they got slowed as one in the group needed frequent breaks and was getting cramps as the altitude climbed to 5,000 feet on Mount Lafayette. The other three apparently trained at the gym for the nine-mile hike. When it started getting dark and the temperatures dropped below freezing, they decided not to take further risks and called 911. They were on Franconia Ridge and it was around 8.30 pm. One of them was having difficulty breathing.But the authorities declared that they were all unprepared and for that reason, the New Hampshire Fish and Game Department may impose a penalty above $1,000 on them. New Hampshire sent a search and rescue team, and it took nine hours to get back to base. A spokesperson said the group "did not have headlamps or enough food and water to complete the 7-9 hour hike. The rescuers located them at 1.15 am and the teens were finally back at 9.07 am Saturday.After the rescue, the 18-year-olds said they were glad that all of them got home safe. "They were stressed for a bit and proud that we helped a friend and had help for him," said Shah. "These things happen very often and people don’t know what will happen up there."
Article Summary: Four Indian-origin teenagers from New Jersey, Jainam Bhavsar, Purva Jayani, Tirth Shah and Advik Yadav, set out on an evening hike in New Hampshire. The incident took place last Friday and they were rescued Saturday after a nine-hour operation by the emergency team. New Hampshire Fish and Game Department may impose a penalty above $1,000 on them.

Article Title: In 1916, a Texas woman left six acres of riverbank for the public; her governor son later added 250 acres and the tiny gift helped create Texas' first state park
Article Text:
Mother Neff State Park (Image Credit: Wikipedia)

A family arrives in Texas

A favourite place by the river

Six acres become a public gift

Her son adds 250 acres

The CCC builds the park

The river remains a challenge

A legacy that grew

In 1916, a small piece of land along Texas’ Leon River became the starting point for what would eventually become the state’s first state park. Isabella Neff, known locally as Mother Neff, had long welcomed neighbours and community groups to the riverbank for picnics, gatherings, fishing and other events. She donated six acres of her favourite spot to the State of Texas for a park in 1916. According to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD), her son, Pat Neff, later expanded the family’s contribution by donating 250 acres to the state in 1934. What followed was the development of Mother Neff State Park, shaped further by the Civilian Conservation Corps and officially opened in 1937.Isabella Eleanor Shepherd was born in Roanoke, Virginia, in 1830. She married Noah Neff in 1854, and after their marriage, the couple decided to move to Texas. Their journey from Roanoke to Belton took 52 days by carriage because they did not travel on Sundays.After spending three months in Belton, the couple moved into a small log cabin near Eagle Springs. There, they raised nine children. Their youngest son, Pat Morris Neff, would later become a teacher, lawyer, governor of Texas and president of Baylor University.The Neff family eventually owned about 900 acres along the Leon River, including the land that would become the park.The land was already a gathering place long before it became a state park. Isabella Neff was well known and respected in the local community, and she regularly invited neighbours and friends to spend time along the river.People came to the shaded riverbanks and grassy areas to picnic, swim and fish. Community groups also asked to use the property for meetings and celebrations. Political rallies, church events, family reunions and other gatherings brought visitors from surrounding communities, with some people camping overnight.One group, the Woodsmen of the World from the nearby Whitson community, had held an annual picnic on the property since 1905. Although the organisation sometimes offered to pay Mother Neff for use of the grounds, she refused. She wanted the place to remain available for community gatherings.Isabella Neff died in May 1921. She had donated six acres of her favourite spot along the river to the State of Texas for use as a park. At the time, Texas did not yet have an official state park system. Her son Pat therefore took responsibility for developing the property. He established what became known as Neff Memorial Park, adding campgrounds, picnic areas and walking trails. The six-acre donation was modest in size, but its significance grew as Texas began developing a formal state park system.The State Parks Board became official in 1923 and began accepting privately donated land into the state system. Pat Neff continued his mother's vision. In 1934, then-Governor Pat Neff donated the family park, totalling 250 acres, to the state. His neighbour Frank Smith also donated 3.5 acres. These contributions transformed the original six-acre gift into a much larger public recreation area. Mother Neff State Park officially opened in 1937.The park's development took another major step during the Great Depression with the arrival of the Civilian Conservation Corps, or CCC. Company 817, made up of more than 200 men, worked at the site from 1934 to 1938. The workers constructed roads, walking trails, picnic areas and campgrounds. They also built several of the structures that would become defining features of the park.Using limestone and other materials from the area, the CCC constructed a pavilion, recreation hall, concession hall and a stone water tower with an observation deck overlooking the valley. Designers, architects and skilled craftsmen worked alongside the young men, helping them develop practical construction skills.The same river that made the area attractive for recreation has also repeatedly created problems. Heavy seasonal rainfall has caused the Leon River to flood, sometimes forcing the park to close for lengthy repairs. CCC planners attempted to protect buildings from floodwaters by raising certain areas. The riverside campground was positioned as high as possible, while the Recreation Hall was built on a mound created by CCC workers.Despite those efforts, severe flooding continued over the years. The park eventually underwent major reconstruction, and a new Park Headquarters and Visitor Center opened in January 2015.Today, Mother Neff State Park covers far more land than the six acres Isabella Neff originally donated. Pat Neff's 250-acre contribution, Frank Smith's 3.5 acres and an additional 142 acres acquired by Texas Parks and Wildlife in 2012 brought the present park to 399 acres.Yet the story of the park still begins with Mother Neff's small gift. She had already treated the riverbank as a place for the community during her lifetime, and her decision to give the land to the public ensured that others could continue enjoying it. The Texas Parks and Wildlife Department now describes Mother Neff State Park as Texas' first state park, crediting the Neff family's generosity and the CCC's work. What began with six acres along a river became a lasting public space and an important part of Texas' conservation history.
Article Summary: Isabella Neff donated six acres of her favourite spot to the State of Texas for a park in 1916. Her son, Pat Neff, later expanded the family’s contribution by donating 250 acres to the state in 1934. Mother Neff State Park officially opened in 1937.

Article Title: US education department tells schools to stop ‘racial balancing’ in student discipline policies
Article Text:
Schools cannot alter discipline rules to cut racial gaps, US Education Dept warns in new guidance.

What does the data show?

The US Education Department has told schools they cannot change student discipline policies solely to reduce racial disparities, arguing that doing so could amount to unlawful discrimination.The guidance, issued by the department's Office for Civil Rights, comes as federal data continues to show that Black students face higher rates of school discipline than their white peers.The department said schools must apply disciplinary rules without treating students differently because of their race. It warned that changing policies specifically to reduce racial differences in disciplinary outcomes would itself constitute race discrimination.“A school's decision to change its discipline policies with the purpose of avoiding or reducing racial disparities in discipline constitutes race discrimination,” the department said in its guidance.A 2023 Education Department report found significant differences in disciplinary rates among students of different races.Black children in public preschools received out-of-school suspensions at a rate nearly twice their share of enrollment, according to the report cited by Reuters.The disparities also continued through K-12 education. Black boys were nearly twice as likely as white boys to receive an out-of-school suspension or expulsion.Black girls were also nearly twice as likely as white girls to receive at least one in-school suspension, out-of-school suspension or expulsion.Eric Duncan, director of P-12 policy at education equity group EdTrust, criticised the new guidance.“You cannot address racial disparities in school discipline by telling schools to ignore race,” Duncan said. “Black students have long faced some of the harshest discipline in our nation's schools.”The latest guidance follows the department's decision last month to remove several disparate-impact regulations that had restricted policies and practices producing discriminatory effects, even when discrimination was not necessarily intended.The changes form part of the Trump administration's wider efforts to roll back diversity initiatives that it argues can result in discrimination based on race or sex.
Article Summary: US Education Dept warns schools they cannot change discipline policies to reduce racial disparities. Department says doing so could amount to unlawful discrimination. Comes as federal data continues to show that Black students face higher rates of school discipline than their white peers. Black children in public preschools received out-of-school suspensions at a rate nearly twice their share of enrollment.

Article Title: Massachusetts police officer accused of using Flock cameras to track her ex-girlfriend; department suspends entire system after her plate was searched a ‘concerning’ number of times
Article Text:
New Bedford suspends use of Flock cameras, officer accused of using system to track ex-girlfriend

Allegations against the police officer

New Bedford suspends Flock camera network

Growing concerns over police surveillance

Police authorities in New Bedford, Massachusetts, have temporarily shut down the city’s entire network of automated license plate reader cameras after allegations that an officer used the system to track the movements of her ex-girlfriend. The New Bedford Police Department suspended its Flock Safety camera system after internal investigators found a "concerning" number of searches linked to a single vehicle’s license plate, according to CBS News Boston. The woman involved told a court hearing that internal affairs officers contacted her after reviewing system access records and asked whether she believed she was being followed. Officer Emily Pacheco, who is at the centre of the investigation, has been placed on administrative leave while an internal affairs inquiry continues. A Massachusetts judge extended an abuse prevention order against Pacheco for six months, finding that she posed a credible threat to her former partner’s physical safety. Under the order, Pacheco had to surrender her personal and department-issued firearms, and her license to carry a firearm was immediately suspended.According to court filings and a signed affidavit obtained by local news outlet The New Bedford Light, the couple ended their two-year relationship in April.The woman later accused Pacheco of repeated harassment, including making "endless calls" and creating fake phone numbers to send text messages. “Showing up to my home unannounced and refuse[d] to leave when asked … saw me pull into my home while on duty, got out of her cruiser and refused to leave,” the woman wrote in the court document, as cited by The New Bedford Light and Them. The affidavit said an internal affairs investigation began after the woman’s license plate was repeatedly searched through the regional surveillance network. Data obtained by local reporters showed that Pacheco was one of the most active users of the city’s Flock camera network this year. In April, the month the relationship ended, Pacheco made 18 searches. The number jumped to 259 in May and 220 in June. Most of the searches were recorded under the general category of "traffic infraction". Department data also showed that some searches reached networks outside New Bedford.During a hearing in Bristol County, Pacheco said she used the surveillance system every day as part of her regular police duties. However, she denied using Flock to watch or track her former girlfriend. When asked, "Did you use the Flock system in your capacity as a New Bedford police officer?", Pacheco answered, "Yes". When asked how often she accessed the system, she said, "daily".Following the hearing and growing public concern, the New Bedford Police Department confirmed that it had suspended the entire Flock camera network across the city. In a statement to CBS News Boston, the department said automated license plate readers can be useful but also recognized the serious risks linked to their use. The department said Flock "can be a valuable investigative tool," while acknowledging that the technology raises "legitimate questions about privacy, access, information sharing, and oversight". Flock Safety cameras use automated license plate recognition technology to record vehicle information, including color, make, model and license plate numbers. The data is uploaded to a central network that can be accessed by law enforcement agencies, providing location information with delays of as little as two minutes. Civil liberties groups have repeatedly warned about the possible misuse of such surveillance systems. In a statement published by The New Bedford Light, Gideon Epstein, a technology expert and counsel with the ACLU of Massachusetts, said systems like Flock give police "an unprecedented ability to track all drivers, regardless of whether drivers are suspected of any wrongdoing". Epstein said allegations that officers had misused surveillance databases for personal reasons "highlight the need for robust, effective democratic oversight, transparency, and accountability mechanisms in law, policy, and police operations procedures".Amid concerns about data privacy and possible police misuse, Flock Safety recently changed its default data retention policy. The company reduced the period for storing vehicle location data from 30 days to seven days. The New Bedford Police Union said it was aware of the investigation involving Pacheco but would not comment further until the internal inquiry is complete. The controversy in New Bedford comes as communities across the United States debate the growing use of high-tech police surveillance. New Bedford city councilors have scheduled public hearings to discuss oversight of the technology and consider formal rules for its use before the camera network is restored. When New Bedford adopted the technology, officers were required to provide a specific law enforcement reason for every search. Personal or improper use of the system violates department policy and can lead to the immediate loss of access, termination of employment and possible criminal charges.
Article Summary: New Bedford suspends use of Flock cameras, officer accused of using system to track ex-girlfriend. Internal investigators found a "concerning" number of searches linked to a single vehicle’s license plate. Officer Emily Pacheco, who is at the centre of the investigation, has been placed on administrative leave.

Article Title: Red-faced Pakistan summons top diplomat over US envoy Gor's J&K remark in Srinagar
Article Text:
US Ambassador Sergio Gor visits Srinagar with J&K CM Omar

Pakistan on Wednesday summoned the top US diplomat Islamabad and lodged a protest after US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India” during his visit to Srinagar on Wednesday.The remarks came as Gor made his first visit to Jammu and Kashmir since taking office and met chief minister Omar Abdullah.Gor’s comments were made during a joint media briefing with Abdullah following their meeting at the chief minister’s residence. “It’s a pleasure to be here. This is an important part of India. I am here, visiting for the first time. It is an incredibly beautiful place. I am thrilled to be here,” the US envoy said.Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for Jammu and Kashmir, saying the US regularly reviews its warnings. He said the Indian government and the Jammu and Kashmir administration had taken steps to improve safety in the region.“I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at,” Gor said, adding that the US would consider whether its existing travel warning should be downgraded.The ambassador also described his meeting with Abdullah as “very good” and said the two sides had discussed ways to deepen economic cooperation and create opportunities benefiting India and the US.Abdullah said the talks focused on what Washington could do for Jammu and Kashmir, while also referring to “certain legacy issues” that would need to be addressed.“We look forward to taking this conversation further,” Abdullah said, adding that he was “very hopeful and optimistic” that engagement between the US and Jammu and Kashmir would “both widen and deepen in the years ahead”.
Article Summary: Pakistan summons top US diplomat Islamabad and lodges a protest. US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India’ Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for J&K.

Article Title: Pakistan govt to challenge SC order to move jailed ex-PM Imran Khan to hospital
Article Text:
'Not within four walls of law': Pak law minister on Khan hospitalisation order

The Shehbaz Sharif-led Pakistan government will challenge the Supreme Court's order directing the transfer of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan to a private hospital, as law minister Azam Nazeer Tarar confirmed in a video message on Wednesday.According to news agency Reuters, the Pakitan Supreme Court had ordered the government to move Khan to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital within two days and allow him access to his personal physician.“This order is not within four walls of the law,” Tarar said in a video statement.He said authorities had reviewed the ruling and decided to approach the court seeking a review. “A convicted prisoner has to be treated either inside the jail or at a public hospital according to law,” Tarar said, adding that the review petition would seek a modification of the order.The move could end hopes of Imran Khan’s family and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), which have repeatedly sought better healthcare and visitation rights for the former PM.It could also trigger public discontent over his treatment in custody.Recently, Imran Khan supporters staged widespread protest over his imprisonment against Islamabad government.Khan, 73, has been jailed in Rawalpindi since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases that he says are politically motivated.He was removed from office in 2022 after falling out with Pakistan's powerful military establishment under army chief Asim Munir's influence.The Supreme Court order came after former president Arif Alvi raised concerns over World Cup winning captain and former PM's medical condition.Alvi also shared Khan's vitals on X.Imran Khan's sons have also repeatedly expressed concern about his deteriorating health, while his lawyers have claimed he suffered significant vision loss in his right eye while in prison.
Article Summary: Pakistani law minister Azam Nazeer Tarar confirms government will challenge the Supreme Court's order. Khan, 73, has been jailed in Rawalpindi since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases. He was removed from office in 2022 after falling out with Pakistan's powerful military establishment.

Article Title: Imran Khan’s sister meets him after 9 months as Pakistan SC orders hospital transfer for jailed ex-PM
Article Text:
Former Pak PM is set to be shifted to a hospital after top court's order over health concerns

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan ’s sister Noreen Niazi met him at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail on Tuesday after a gap of around nine months, following a Supreme Court order allowing weekly meetings between the former prime minister and his family amid concerns over his health.The meeting lasted around 15 minutes, according to jail sources, cited by Express Tribune. Noreen briefed Imran on the Supreme Court’s order regarding his transfer to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital and enquired about his health. The two also discussed ongoing legal matters.Noreen confirmed after the meeting that she had met her brother but did not speak to the media, in line with an assurance given before the court. She later left Adiala Jail with her sisters Aleema Khan and Uzma Khan.Imran also met his wife, Bushra Bibi, with their meeting lasting around 30-35 minutes. Bushra earlier met her daughter, Mubashra Sheikh, and sister-in-law Mehrunnisa.Before entering the jail, Noreen told reporters that she would inform Imran that “the Supreme Court has granted you permission” to meet his family. She also said she would brief him about efforts made by PTI workers on his behalf.The meetings followed a three-member Supreme Court bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed directing the government to facilitate weekly meetings between Imran and his family. The court was hearing petitions concerning his access to his sisters and personal physicians, as well as his medical condition.The order came after a medical board report and a report by the Adiala Jail superintendent were submitted to the court. The reports recommended more frequent meetings with Imran’s immediate family and spouse to help manage his blood pressure and anxiety.The Supreme Court also ordered that Imran be moved to Shifa International Hospital for treatment and directed the formation of a medical board comprising an eye specialist, general physician, cardiologist and his personal physician, Dr Faisal Sultan. Dr Uzma was also to be included in the board.The court ordered that his medical records remain confidential and barred political activity or media interactions outside the hospital. It also directed authorities to arrange telephone contact between Imran and his children.Justice Waheed stressed that access to family could not be treated as a favour, describing the meetings as a fundamental right rather than a concession. The court, however, required PTI representatives to refrain from political activity or media engagement after meeting Imran, a condition the party said it would follow.Aleema Khan welcomed the order, saying the family had been demanding hospital treatment for Imran for months. Speaking to reporters at the Dahgal checkpoint in Rawalpindi, she said she was happy about the meeting but remained uncertain about whether the development signalled a broader change in circumstances.“"Words cannot describe how happy I am about the meeting. I cannot even imagine where I would have got sweets from. I have appeared before the ATC Rawalpindi from the Supreme Court,” Aleema said.She also rejected suggestions that the family was politicising Imran’s health, saying they were speaking as his sisters.PTI spokesperson Niazullah Khan Niazi said Imran had a right to meet his family twice a week but that authorities had continued to restrict access despite an Islamabad High Court order. He said the party would comply with the Supreme Court’s direction against political statements after meetings.Concerns over Imran’s health have intensified in recent months. A medical report submitted to the Supreme Court said he had experienced fluctuating blood pressure, palpitations, headaches, restlessness and significant anxiety.A PIMS cardiologist who examined him on August 1 recorded his blood pressure at 140/100mmHg and recommended measures to reduce mental stress, including more frequent meetings with his wife and access to reading material. A four-member medical board that examined him on August 10 recorded his blood pressure at 140/80mmHg and recommended walking, relaxation and more frequent interaction with his immediate family and spouse.The report said Imran had undergone at least 39 medical check-ups since his incarceration, with jail medical officers examining him three times a day. It also said his ECG was normal and his vision had improved to almost normal following treatment for an eye condition.PTI has questioned the authenticity and completeness of the medical documentation and demanded examinations by Imran’s personal physicians, Dr Asim Yusuf and Dr Faisal Sultan, as well as an independent medical board. The government has rejected claims that he is being denied proper medical care, saying he is receiving treatment from specialists in accordance with the law and court orders.A report submitted to the Supreme Court in February had said Imran’s right eye was functioning at only 15% capacity. The court subsequently ordered that he be granted access to his personal physicians in Adiala Jail.Imran and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. They were sentenced in December 2025 to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case over allegations that they unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince.Imran has been in custody since August 2023, initially following his conviction in the £190 million corruption case. He also faces pending trials under Pakistan’s Anti-Terrorism Act in connection with the May 9, 2023, protests.Imran, who served as prime minister from 2018 until his ouster through a parliamentary no-confidence vote in 2022, and his supporters have consistently maintained that the cases against him are politically motivated and aimed at preventing his political comeback.
Article Summary: Imran's sister Noreen Niazi met him at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail on Tuesday after a gap of around nine months. Meeting followed a Supreme Court order allowing weekly meetings between the former prime minister and his family amid concerns over his health.

Article Title: 'Move Imran Khan to hospital': Pakistan Supreme Court directs govt amid ex-PM's health concerns
Article Text:
Pakistan SC orders Imran Khan’s hospital transfer. photo credit: AP

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe Imran Khan should receive immediate medical attention? Yes, he needs immediate care No, he can stay in jail Unsure, need more information 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan’s Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the government to move imprisoned former prime minister Imran Khan to a hospital, meeting a longstanding demand from his party and family amid growing concerns over his health.Khan, 73, has been in jail since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases that he and his supporters have described as politically motivated. His Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party welcomed the court order, saying it should have come earlier.“It’s a very welcome order and we wish it had happened sooner so his eye and general health would not have deteriorated this much,” PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari told Reuters.“He should remain in hospital until all doctors are satisfied,” Bukhari added.According to Khan’s spokesperson Naeem Haider Panjutha, the court directed that he be moved to Shifa International Hospital within 48 hours and remain there until September 16.Also Read: 'Needs to be moved to hospital now': Imran Khan's health in jail deteriorates The order came amid renewed concerns over Khan’s physical and mental health. His sons, Sulaiman Khan and Kasim Khan, have repeatedly raised concerns about his access to family, lawyers and doctors.“We have no updates because his family, doctors and lawyers haven’t been allowed to see him for seven months,” they told CNN earlier this month.The development came after former Pakistani president Arif Alvi also said on Tuesday that Khan’s medical reports were “alarming”, citing concerns over anxiety, palpitations and high blood pressure.In a post on X, Alvi said, “Imran Khan’s medical reports are alarming. I have gone through them with several specialists, and I am writing this in plain language so every Pakistani can understand exactly what is happening.”Alvi said the issues that concerned him most were Khan’s “anxiety and stress levels”, “palpitations,” and “high blood pressure”.Alvi also raised concerns over Khan’s heart rate and called for further medical monitoring, including a 24-hour Holter monitor.“I am deeply worried. Isolation is taking a physical toll on his body. If this is not addressed immediately, the damage may become irreversible with more complications to follow,” Alvi said.Calling for Khan to be hospitalised, the former president said: “@ImranKhanPTI definitely needs to be moved to a hospital environment now, under an independent panel of doctors.”Khan’s legal troubles intensified after his ouster as prime minister in a no-confidence vote in 2022. He has faced multiple cases, including those involving state gifts and an unlawful marriage, with some convictions suspended or overturned and appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing.The PTI, which came to power in 2018 and retains a significant support base, was stripped of its election symbol before the 2024 general election, forcing its candidates to contest as independents.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court orders former prime minister Imran Khan to be moved to a hospital. Khan has been in jail since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases. His party welcomed the court order, saying it should have come earlier. The order came amid renewed concerns over Khan’s physical and mental health.

Article Title: 'Needs to be moved to hospital now': Imran Khan's health in jail deteriorates
Article Text:
Alvi warns over Imran Khan’s worsening health

NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan President Arif Alvi on Tuesday raised the alarm over jailed ex-PM Imran Khan’s worsening health, saying his medical reports were “alarming” and pointing to anxiety, heart palpitations and high blood pressure.In a post on X, Alvi said, "Imran Khan's medical reports are alarming. I have gone through them with several specialists, and I am writing this in plain language so every Pakistani can understand exactly what is happening."Alvi said the issues that concerned him most were Khan's "anxiety and stress levels", "palpitations," and "high blood pressure." He added that while sleeplessness was not mentioned in the report, Khan's medication appeared to suggest the problem."I have known Imran Khan for more than 35 years. Stress was never his weakness. That it is now at peak levels tells you everything about what three years of imprisonment and total isolation have done to him," he said.Alvi attributed Khan's stress to the political situation in Pakistan, the imprisonment and deaths of his colleagues, his own prolonged isolation and limited access to newspapers, books and information from outside.He also raised concerns over former PM and the only world-cup winning cricket captain Imran Khan's heart rate, which he said had increased to 54 beats per minute (bpm), compared with his historically lower resting rate."His heart rate is 54 bpm. Doctors will call that 'normal.' It is not normal for him," Alvi said, adding that Khan had also reported heart palpitations.Alvi called for Khan to undergo immediate cardiac monitoring, saying he "needs a 24-hour Holter monitor immediately". He also urged regular monitoring of his blood pressure.He recommended several tests, including a stress test, echocardiogram, cardiac MRI, cardiac artery calcium scan and cardiac CT angiogram, along with any other tests doctors may consider necessary."I am deeply worried. Isolation is taking a physical toll on his body. If this is not addressed immediately, the damage may become irreversible with more complications to follow," Alvi said.Calling for Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Khan to be shifted to a hospital, Alvi said, "Imran Khan definitely needs to be moved to a hospital environment now, under an independent panel of doctors.""Neither his family nor the people of Pakistan trust government-appointed doctors alone," he added."The next three months will decide whether his condition is reversed or becomes permanent," Alvi said. He further said, "We all are alarmed. The country needs him more than ever before."Khan remains behind bars, while his sons, Sulaiman Khan and Kasim Khan, have also raised concerns about their father's access to his family, lawyers and doctors."We have no updates because his family, doctors and lawyers haven't been allowed to see him for seven months," they told CNN earlier this month.The statements came amid nationwide demonstrations by supporters of Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), who have demanded the release of the former prime minister and his wife, Bushra Bibi.Khan served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 until his ouster through a parliamentary no-confidence vote in 2022. He has been imprisoned since 2023 following convictions in several cases, including graft charges and the alleged disclosure of official secrets.Khan and his political aides have consistently alleged that the cases against him are politically motivated and intended to prevent his return to politics.After his ouster, Khan led nationwide rallies alleging that the government of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had conspired with Pakistan's military establishment and Washington to remove him. The subsequent crackdown targeted PTI leaders and supporters, while the party was barred from contesting the 2024 general elections.Khan's supporters have repeatedly maintained that the legal proceedings against him are politically motivated and aimed at blocking his political comeback.
Article Summary: Former Pakistan President Arif Alvi raises alarm over jailed ex-PM Imran Khan’s worsening health. Alvi says Khan's medical reports were “alarming” and pointed to anxiety, heart palpitations and high blood pressure. He also raised concerns over former PM's heart rate, which he said had increased to 54 beats per minute.

Article Title: '30 civilans killed': Baloch activist shares video of 'Pakistani war crime', seeks US intervention
Article Text:
Mir Yar Baloch has urged the US administration to impose sanctions on Pakistan.

Baloch leader seeks US sanctions

ALSO READ |

Pakistan disputes airstrike allegations

Protests erupt over reported civilian deaths

ALSO READ |

Mir Yar Baloch, a Baloch leader, has accused Pakistan 's military of carrying out an airstrike in Balochistan that allegedly killed 30 civilians, including women, children and infants.He claimed that video footage from the August 12 attack in Surab's Gidar Goandhan area provides evidence of the military operation and said he plans to take the matter to the International Criminal Court."The Republic of Balochistan has obtained video footage of the Surab Air Strike conducted by the external terrorist forces of Pakistan on 12th August, which killed 30 innocent Balochistan civilians including women, children, and infants and injured dozens more. The missile debris clearly visible in the video constitute irrefutable proof of Pakistan's terrorism. They also thoroughly expose Pakistan's military spokesperson, DG ISPR, who deliberately misled the global community on national media by claiming the attack was merely an IED blast on the ground," Mir Yar Baloch wrote on X.Mir Yar Baloch has urged the US administration to impose sanctions on Pakistan and halt military support, including F-16 engine spare parts and upgrades to fighter jets and missile programmes."The Republic of Balochistan urges the Trump administration to impose strict economic sanctions on Pakistan, cancel the delivery of spare parts for F-16 engines, and halt all upgradation package to its fighter jets and missile program.The Pakistan military and air force are massively employing these very weapons and aircraft against the people of the independent Republic of Balochistan. Washington must hold Pakistan fully accountable for its war crimes in Balochistan," he added.The two sides have given sharply different accounts of what happened in Surab, leaving the circumstances of the incident and the actual civilian death toll disputed.Pakistan's military has rejected the claim of an airstrike and said the casualties were caused by a premature explosion involving a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device allegedly being assembled by militants.The Inter-Services Public Relations said the initial blast killed eight militants and that a secondary explosion involving other explosives stored at the site also caused civilian deaths."However, the blast and secondary detonation of other explosives stored there by the terrorists of Indian Proxy have also reportedly caused tragic casualties of three nearby civilians," the ISPR said.The military said Pakistani forces and Balochistan Police subsequently killed 10 more individuals, taking the reported militant death toll to 18. Two Pakistani soldiers were also injured during the exchange of fire.The competing accounts have come amid protests in Balochistan following reports of civilian deaths in the Surab area.The Balochistan Post reported that more than 20 people were initially killed and at least 16 injured in the incident. Some local residents, however, claimed that the actual death toll could be higher.
Article Summary: Baloch leader Mir Yar Baloch has accused Pakistan's military of carrying out an airstrike in Balochistan that allegedly killed 30 civilians. He claims that video footage from the August 12 attack in Surab's Gidar Goandhan area provides evidence of the military operation. He has urged the US administration to impose sanctions on Pakistan.

Article Title: Pakistani minister in Balochistan province escapes armed attack on convoy
Article Text:
All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official.​

Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy in Mastung district on Friday, injuring six people, including three police personnel.The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said."Six people were injured in the attack, but the minister remained unhurt and the convoy has returned to Quetta," Rind said.All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official. Three of them were police personnel, with two reportedly in serious condition. They were taken to a hospital in Quetta for treatment.The attack has raised fresh security concerns in Khad Kocha, an area that has repeatedly come under attack in recent weeks.According to officials, this was the fourth attack on travellers along the same highway since last month. Insurgents have repeatedly targeted people travelling through the area despite a major security operation carried out following the earlier incidents.Security forces have now sealed off the area and launched a search operation to locate those responsible for the latest attack.The incident adds to the continuing security challenges in Balochistan, where armed insurgent groups have carried out attacks against security forces and civilians.
Article Summary: Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy. The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat. All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official.

Article Title: 'Water is our red line': Shehbaz Sharif threatens India with 'direct response' over Indus Treaty
Article Text:
Shehbaz Sharif speaking on eve of Pakistan's Independence Day

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the Indus Waters Treaty be renegotiated? Yes, it needs changes No, it should remain unchanged 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan has yet again raked up India’s suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), with its Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif threatening a “direct response” to New Delhi’s move, which came days after the Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir in April last year."The Prime Minister said that India has proven itself an enemy of peace by unilaterally and illegally suspending the Indus Waters Treaty. He announced that every drop of Pakistan's water is our red line. There will be no compromise on the water issue. If India does not come to the right path, we will give it a direct response," the Pakistan Prime Minister's Office said in a statement on X.Sharif, speaking at an event on the eve of Pakistan’s Independence Day (August 14), sought to portray India as an “enemy of peace” over New Delhi’s decision to keep the IWT in abeyance following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 civilians were killed.He said New Delhi had proved itself an “enemy” of peace by putting the treaty in abeyance."India proved itself an enemy of peace by unilaterally and illegally suspending the Indus Waters Treaty. I declare in clear terms that every single drop of Pakistan's water is our red line. If India does not come to its senses, it will be responded to directly," the Pakistani premier added.The military hostilities ended on May 10 after Islamabad sought a ceasefire following India’s air strikes on multiple Pakistani air bases.The conflict erupted after India's Operation Sindoor in retaliation for the Pahalgam attack.New Delhi kept the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance after a Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) meeting on April 23, 2025, and asserted that the conditions under which the treaty was negotiated have "fundamentally changed."India has asserted the treaty can no longer function in its present form and will remain in abeyance until Pakistan “credibly and irrevocably” ends its support for cross-border terrorism.The Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) was signed in September 1960.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif threatens a "direct response" to India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty. The move came days after the Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir in April last year. New Delhi kept the IWT in abeyance after a Cabinet Committee on Security meeting on April 23, 2025.

Article Title: Why US is questioning Pakistan's Rs 3 trillion defence spending
Article Text:
The US also criticised Islamabad for not publishing its executive budget proposal within a reasonable period (representative image)

US asks Pakistan to improve defence and debt transparency

Pakistan's defence allocation rises to Rs 3 trillion

Defence spending remains a key transparency concern

The US state department has flagged a lack of adequate parliamentary and civilian oversight of Pakistan's military and intelligence spending, while also raising concerns over limited disclosure of government debt and delays in publishing the executive budget proposal.The concerns were highlighted in the 2026 Fiscal Transparency Report, which assessed Pakistan's public financial transparency and identified gaps in the country's budgetary and fiscal disclosure practices.The report noted that Pakistan made its enacted budget and end-of-year financial statements widely available online. However, it said military and intelligence budgets remained outside adequate parliamentary or civilian public scrutiny.“The military and intelligence budgets were not subject to adequate parliamentary or civilian public oversight,” the report said.The US also criticised Islamabad for not publishing its executive budget proposal within a reasonable period.According to the assessment, this limits the time available for lawmakers and civil society to examine government spending before the budget is adopted.The state department called for three key changes to Pakistan's fiscal transparency framework.It urged Islamabad to make its executive budget proposal publicly available within a reasonable period, disclose detailed information about government debt obligations, including liabilities linked to state-owned enterprises, and bring military and intelligence agency budgets under parliamentary or civilian public oversight.The report also raised concerns about Pakistan's disclosure of public debt, saying only limited information was available on debt obligations, including those of major state-owned enterprises.At the same time, the US assessment acknowledged some positive aspects of Pakistan's public financial system.It said the country's supreme audit institution met international standards of independence and noted that its audit reports were published in a timely manner and contained substantive findings.The US assessment comes against the backdrop of a substantial increase in Pakistan's defence allocation for the 2026-27 financial year.In June, Pakistan's federal government proposed allocating Rs 3 trillion for defence services, up 17.65 per cent from the previous year's initial allocation of Rs 2.55 trillion, according to Dawn.The proposed defence services allocation amounts to about 2.08 per cent of Pakistan's projected GDP of Rs 143.6 trillion and nearly 16 per cent of the federal government's total outlay of Rs 18.77 trillion.Spending on civil works related to military infrastructure was projected to rise 7.92 per cent to Rs 363.16 billion, from Rs 336.49 billion previously.Military pensions are accounted for separately from the main defence services budget. The government has allocated Rs 822 billion for retired military personnel under the federal pension outlay, according to Dawn.The allocation for defence administration was set at Rs 10.9 billion, compared with Rs 7.9 billion in the outgoing fiscal year's original budget. That allocation was later revised to Rs 11.75 billion.Major military imports and defence acquisitions are generally funded outside the main defence services allocation and remain undisclosed.The US state department's assessment therefore highlights a distinction between Pakistan's publicly disclosed defence allocation and the wider military spending that may not be fully visible through the country's budgetary documents.The state department's recommendations focus on bringing military and intelligence expenditure into the broader framework of public financial oversight.While the report recognised that Pakistan publishes key budget documents, it identified defence and intelligence spending, debt disclosure and the timing of budget publication as areas requiring greater transparency.The recommendations would require Pakistan to give lawmakers and the public greater visibility into military and intelligence allocations, as well as government liabilities linked to state-owned enterprises.
Article Summary: US asks Pakistan to improve defence and debt transparency. Pakistan's defence allocation rises to Rs 3 trillion for 2026-27 financial year. US state department flagged a lack of adequate parliamentary and civilian oversight of Pakistan's military and intelligence spending. Report also raised concerns over limited disclosure of government debt and delays in publishing executive budget proposal.

Article Title: PML-N set to form 'government' in PoK after two former 'premiers' lose strongholds in third phase
Article Text:
Two former PoK premiers lost their strongholds in the third phase of elections marred by violence and rigging allegations, as the PML-N emerged dominant

Two former so-called prime ministers of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) lost their traditional strongholds in the third phase of elections, according to unofficial results released on Tuesday, while incumbent premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore of the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) retained his seat.The latest results came after voting in four constituencies on Monday, with the election process again overshadowed by violence and allegations of rigging. Polling in the remaining seven constituencies was postponed over concerns about the law-and-order situation and is expected to be held on August 21, according to the region's election commission.The PPP won two of the four seats contested in the third phase, while the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party won one each. The latter is backed by both Jamaat-e-Islami and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).Former prime minister and Muslim Conference president Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan, who was backed by the PML-N, lost the seat in Western Bagh's Dhirkot constituency to Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party candidate Sardar Sajid Iqbal, according to unofficial results. The seat had been held by the Muslim Conference/PML-N since 1985.In Central Bagh, PPP's Zia Qamar retained the seat, defeating PML-N candidate Mushtaq Minhas.Former premier Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, who joined the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party, secured only a few thousand votes.The result in Eastern Bagh remained pending after authorities ordered a re-poll at 12 polling stations. PML-N candidate Sardar Mir Akbar was leading based on results from 174 of the constituency's 186 polling stations, followed by PPP candidate Sardar Qamaruz Zaman Khan.The election comes against the backdrop of a striking shift in the Pakistani government's treatment of the protest movement that has rocked PoK for months.Just days before the final phase of voting, Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif had described the protesters as "enemies of Pakistan" and ruled out talks with them. But Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's adviser Rana Sanaullah subsequently said 99% of those associated with the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) were "patriotic brothers", promising that a PML-N government would engage with the group and seek to resolve its demands.The reversal in rhetoric came as the PML-N emerged as the dominant force in the election and prepared to form the next government in the region. The party has secured 25 of the 45 directly elected seats so far, while the PPP has won 12 and the Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party one.The first two phases, held on July 27 and August 2, were also marked by violent protests and allegations of widespread rigging, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. Supporters of the two parties clashed at several polling stations.The JAAC has been protesting across the region since early June, with demands including the abolition of 12 refugee seats that it says can be used to influence the formation of governments in PoK.The group has alleged that more than 40 people were killed during violence surrounding the first phase of voting and that around 400 protesters had been killed since the protests began. The Pakistani government has rejected the higher figure as exaggerated, while Sanaullah has acknowledged that deaths from the unrest were in the "double figures".India does not recognise Pakistan's control over the territory, maintaining that Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are integral and inalienable parts of India and describing Pakistan's presence in areas under its control as "illegal and forcible occupation".
Article Summary: Two former so-called prime ministers of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) lost their traditional strongholds in the third phase of elections. Incumbent premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore of the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) retained his seat. Polling in the remaining seven constituencies was postponed over concerns about the law-and-order situation.

Article Title: 'Discontent answered with bullets': MEA slams Pakistan over PoK crackdown
Article Text:
